title: Pros and Cons
text: Pros and Cons. It looks good once it is together. The together part is the problem. The starter holes for the clamps that allow this to be put together and then taken apart, are marked, but aren't anywhere close to lining up with the holes in the clamps.  That little snafu causes a larger problem. This isn't a folding table in the normal manner. The top is actually a separate piece that needs to be totally removed so that you can fold in the sides. Then you can lay it flat and store the 2 pieces together. THEY ARE NOT CONNECTED.  Because the starter holes for the clamps don't line up, if there is variation in the clamp placement, the top is difficult to get on and off. In fact I didn't think I would be able to get the top on. It would connect to 3 of the 4 clamps. So I took it of and tried it in a different rotation and finally got the top on. That last connection is hard though.  Once it is together is is sturdy, but frankly it isn't easy to take apart and put together. If that's what you are looking for this isn't it.
